ground_truth.title: State v. Michael Ortega
ground_truth.charge: Computer Fraud and Unauthorized Access to Information Systems

defendant.name: Michael Ortega
defendant.background: Owner of the dockside pharmacy "Maritime Meds" and longtime resident of Port Haven

victim.name: Eleanor Voss
victim.description: Owner of Port Haven Marina, 55, responsible for client contracts and dock operations

ground_truth.what_really_happened: On the evening of May 9, 2024, Michael Ortega accessed the marina’s client database through his office laptop, using an administrative account he was not authorized to use. He copied sensitive client information onto a USB drive and later transferred it to an external server. The marina’s IT system logged an unauthorized login from Ortega’s office IP address. The stolen data was subsequently sold on a dark‑web forum the following week. Ortega was caught by the police after the marina notified authorities of the breach.

timeline.event: Ortega logs into marina database using administrative credentials
Ortega copies client records to USB drive
Ortega transfers data to external server
Marina IT logs unauthorized access from Ortega's office IP
Marina owner Eleanor Voss reports data breach to police

evidence.name: Hard Drive Copy
evidence.description: Investigators recovered a copy of the marina database from Ortega’s office laptop showing modified timestamps and deleted records
evidence.truth_note: The hard drive was physically seized from Ortega’s office, proving his device held the corrupted data

evidence.name: Surveillance Footage
evidence.description: CCTV from Dock 3 shows Ortega entering the marina office alone at 18:05 and exiting with a sealed USB drive
evidence.truth_note: Footage captured Ortega’s movements directly linking him to the time of the unauthorized access

evidence.name: IP Log File
evidence.description: Marina server logs an unauthorized login at 18:00 from the IP address registered to Ortega’s pharmacy
evidence.truth_note: The IP address was tied to Ortega’s office network, confirming his device performed the access

evidence.name: Phishing Email Draft
evidence.description: A draft of a phishing email was found in Ortega’s personal Gmail, addressed to a marina employee
evidence.truth_note: The email draft contains a link identical to the one used to download the stolen data, indicating premeditation

evidence.name: Dockworker Testimony
evidence.description: Witness statement from dockworker Lisa Marquez noting Ortega’s presence near the office at the time of the breach
evidence.truth_note: Lisa saw Ortega walking toward the office after hours and did not observe any other suspicious activity

evidence.name: Security Guard Alibi
evidence.description: Security guard records show the guard on duty at Dock 3 had a scheduled break from 17:45 to 18:30, allowing Ortega access
evidence.truth_note: The guard’s break coincides with the breach window, indicating a gap in supervision rather than evidence of Ortega’s innocence

evidence.name: USB Drive Physical Analysis
evidence.description: USB drive seized from Ortega’s office contains a forensic image of the stolen database
evidence.truth_note: While the USB drive belongs to Ortega, the forensic image could have been inserted by a third party; the chain of custody for the drive is well documented

witnesses.name: Lisa Marquez
witnesses.role: dockworker and competitor of Ortega’s pharmacy
witnesses.knows: Saw Ortega near the office at 18:00 and heard no other individuals in the vicinity
witnesses.bias: Competitive bias due to business rivalry; may emphasize Ortega’s suspicious presence

witnesses.name: Thomas Riley
witnesses.role: security guard for Port Haven Marina
witnesses.knows: The guard’s break schedule and that the security camera feed was inactive during 18:05–18:20
witnesses.bias: Neutral; duty to report factual operations
